lead: >-
  A tour through Chiclayo offers a chance to explore the archaeological treasures of northern Peru as part of a journey across the country. After Lima, Machu Picchu, Lake Titicaca and Colca Canyon, the route continues to Trujillo and Chiclayo, revealing the heritage of the Chimú and Moche cultures. Here is how long the northern leg takes, what the confirmed itinerary includes and who will enjoy this journey.
---

## Tours through Chiclayo: why northern Peru is worth exploring

**[Chiclayo](/peru/place/chiclayo/) is a destination for anyone interested in the history of Peru's northern civilizations.** The surrounding region is home to Moche archaeological sites and discoveries associated with the Lord of Sipán. They reveal a different chapter of the country's past from the Inca stonework in [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/).

{{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passes through Chiclayo. In our itinerary, northern Peru is the final leg of a **14-day journey**. Before reaching it, travelers explore Lima, the Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu, Lake Titicaca, Colca Canyon and Arequipa.

The [Peru tour featuring Trujillo and Chiclayo](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-arequipa-puno-trujillo-chiclayo/) is designed for travelers who want to discover several historical eras on one trip. If Chiclayo is your only goal, this itinerary is considerably broader than necessary: much of the journey takes place in southern and central Peru.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_ves_mnogolikij_peru_i_senor_sipan}}

## How Chiclayo fits into the 14-day itinerary

Days 12 and 13 are devoted to the northern region. It is useful to distinguish between visiting Chiclayo itself, exploring nearby archaeological sites and stopping at places along the road: these are separate parts of the itinerary.

| Day | Main activities |
|---|---|
| 12 | Flight to Trujillo, Chan Chan, Huanchaco, road transfer to Chiclayo |
| 13 | Sipán archaeological sites, then flight to Lima |

### Day 12: Trujillo, Chan Chan and the journey to Chiclayo

After the flight from Lima to [Trujillo](/peru/place/trujillo/), the itinerary continues to [Chan Chan](/peru/place/chan-chan/). This vast archaeological complex of adobe buildings is associated with the Chimú culture. Its walls and reliefs show just how different the architecture of Peru's northern coast was from Inca stone terraces in the Andes.

The same day includes the coastal suburb of Huanchaco and the Temples of the Sun and Moon. In the evening, travelers drive to Chiclayo and check into a hotel. **The overnight stay in Chiclayo comes after a full day of excursions around Trujillo.** There is therefore little opportunity to plan a major independent exploration of Chiclayo that evening.

For more information about the ancient city, see our dedicated [Chan Chan page](/peru/place/chan-chan/). It is particularly useful for travelers more interested in archaeology than general city sightseeing.

### Day 13: Sipán and the return to Lima

After breakfast, excursions take place around Chiclayo. The itinerary names the Lord of Sipán Museum, [Huaca Rajada](/peru/place/huaca-rajada/) and the Sipán Museum. A transfer to the airport and flight to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) follow.

Understanding the difference between the two main attractions makes the visit more rewarding. **Huaca Rajada** is the archaeological site where researchers discovered the richly furnished tomb of a Moche ruler. The Royal Tombs of Sipán Museum in Lambayeque displays finds including jewelry and ceremonial burial objects. Seeing the excavation site and its museum collection provides complementary perspectives: first the place where the tomb was found, then the artifacts that helped reconstruct the ruler's story.

Other important sites in the region, such as the pyramids of Túcume and the Sicán complex, are not automatically included in this tour. The scheduled visits on this day concern the Sipán sites specifically.

## How northern Peru differs from Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley

Comparing these regions helps explain the appeal of an extended Peru itinerary.

| Region | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Cusco and the Sacred Valley | Inca heritage, stone architecture, the Andes |
| Trujillo and Chiclayo | Moche and Chimú civilizations, adobe complexes, museums |

In the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), the itinerary connects archaeological structures and mountain settlements. The northern leg reveals the material culture of coastal societies that flourished long before the arrival of the Incas. The contrast in building techniques is especially revealing: mountain terraces and stone masonry versus the earthen walls of Chan Chan.

There is a practical difference, too. Cusco, Lake Titicaca and Colca Canyon are at high altitude, whereas Chiclayo lies in the lowlands near the coast. During one journey, travelers encounter different temperatures, physical demands and types of transport. When choosing the full itinerary, pay particular attention to **the high-altitude days in the Andes**, not just the excursions on the northern coast.

You can find other journeys focused on Inca heritage in the [Peru tour catalog](/peru/tour/). For an archaeological emphasis, see the [cultural and historical tours in Peru](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/).

## Logistics: why Chiclayo comes near the end

The itinerary begins with the capital and the sights of southern Peru, followed by a separate flight from Lima to Trujillo. After visiting archaeological complexes, travelers drive overland to Chiclayo and fly back to Lima the following day. This avoids having to cross the entire country again by road after the northern leg.

The confirmed tour inclusions cover domestic flights **Lima–Cusco, Arequipa–Lima, Lima–Trujillo and Chiclayo–Lima**, as well as excursions with a Russian-speaking interpreter. The itinerary also includes an Expedition-class train ticket for the Machu Picchu section. Accommodation, meals and additional expenses are detailed on the [14-day tour page](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-arequipa-puno-trujillo-chiclayo/).

This is an intensive journey, with historic centers, high-altitude destinations, flights and excursions following one another. Travelers choose it for its broad coverage of Peru. If you prefer a relaxed stay in a single region, shorter itineraries and a separately arranged visit to Chiclayo may be more suitable.

## Choosing a journey that visits Chiclayo

**For a first extensive trip around Peru**, the existing 14-day tour is a good choice if Machu Picchu, Lake Titicaca, Colca Canyon and northern archaeology all appeal to you. Consider the number of transfers and the need to acclimatize in the Andes.

**For a focused archaeological journey in the north**, build the itinerary around Trujillo, Chan Chan, Huaca Rajada and the museums of Lambayeque. This is a different style of trip; a separate ready-made northern-only tour is not currently listed in this selection. When discussing a custom itinerary, specify the sites you want to see and how much time you would like in each city.

Exact stops and confirmed excursions matter more than the general label “archaeological.” An interest in the Sipán Museum and a desire to explore the pyramids of Túcume in depth, for example, call for different schedules. Check the named sites in the itinerary and arrange additional visits separately.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Chiclayo

### How much time do travelers spend in Chiclayo?

On the current 14-day itinerary, travelers arrive in Chiclayo on the evening of day 12. After an overnight stay, day 13 is dedicated to the Sipán sites and a flight back to Lima. It is a short stop centered on a specific excursion program.

### Does the tour include Chan Chan?

Yes. [Chan Chan](/peru/place/chan-chan/) is visited on the day of arrival in Trujillo, before the road transfer to Chiclayo. Huanchaco and the Temples of the Sun and Moon are scheduled for the same day.

### Does the itinerary include Machu Picchu?

Yes. [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) features earlier in the journey. Northern Peru, including Trujillo and Chiclayo, follows the Andes and Colca Canyon.

### Can Túcume or other archaeological sites be added?

Túcume is a separate archaeological attraction in the Lambayeque region. The published itinerary for days 12–13 does not mention a visit to Túcume. Adding it should be discussed as an itinerary change, allowing for travel time and the subsequent flight.

### Is the tour suitable for travelers interested only in northern Peru?

The existing itinerary covers nearly all of Peru's classic travel regions and involves numerous internal transfers. A trip primarily focused on the north would require a separate itinerary with a different distribution of days.

## Chinchero in Peru's Sacred Valley: textiles, Inca heritage and the Sunday market

Chinchero is located in the mountains near [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), on the way to the Sacred Valley of the Incas. The settlement is known for its archaeological remains, traditional textiles and Sunday market, where visitors can see the work of local craftspeople. Unlike larger tourism centers, Chinchero offers a glimpse of both historical monuments and everyday life in an Andean community.

The village sits on a high-altitude plateau, making it cooler than the lower parts of the valley. Walks reveal views of terraced hillsides and mountain peaks. Visiting as part of a Sacred Valley excursion is convenient, especially when other settlements and archaeological sites in the area are included.

## Inca terraces and Túpac Yupanqui's palace

Chinchero's historical complex is associated with the Inca ruler Túpac Yupanqui. Stone foundations, fragments of walls and agricultural terraces have survived here, while colonial-era buildings were later constructed on parts of the older structures.

It is a vivid example of several historical periods sharing the same place. Beside masonry made from large stone blocks, you can see church architecture and urban buildings that emerged after the Spanish conquest. Pay particular attention to the arrangement of terraces along the hillside and the forms of the stonework.

Admission to the archaeological area depends on the applicable tourist ticket and site rules. Chinchero has its own access restrictions; a ticket to an individual museum in Cusco does not necessarily grant entry to every historic site in the valley.

## Weaving: from wool to finished cloth

Chinchero is considered one of the centers of traditional textile craftsmanship in the Cusco region. Local craftswomen demonstrate how fibers are prepared, spun, dyed and woven into patterns. Some workshops display looms and finished woolen products.

For visitors, it is particularly interesting to discover how fabrics get their colors. Traditional techniques use plants and other natural dyes, and patterns can reflect local motifs. Every workshop has its own methods, so it is best to confirm the demonstration program in advance.

Buying textiles can be a way to learn about the craft and support individual artisans, but check the quality, fiber composition, handmade origin and price with the seller. Not every souvenir sold at the market was necessarily made in this village.

## Chinchero's Sunday market

A market takes place in the main square on Sundays, described by Peru's official tourism portal as one of the Sacred Valley's notable markets. Stalls offer textiles, hats, scarves, local foods and Andean agricultural produce. Elements of traditional commerce survive here, and bartering is sometimes seen.

The market is livelier on Sundays than on other days. Visitors can come for architecture and textile workshops throughout the week, but the full Sunday market does not operate every day.

| Reason for visiting | Recommended activity |
|---|---|
| History | Inca archaeological complex |
| Crafts | Textile workshop |
| Traditional commerce | Sunday market |

If you plan to shop, it is useful to carry local currency in small denominations. Ask artisans and vendors before photographing them, particularly while they are working.

## Chinchero and other places in the Sacred Valley

Chinchero is often visited on the journey between Cusco and Urubamba. Nearby are [Pisac](/peru/place/pisac/) and [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/), although their attractions differ: Pisac is known for its extensive terraces and archaeological remains, while Ollantaytambo features an Inca-planned town and monumental complex. Chinchero is especially famous for its textiles and craft heritage.

The [eight-day “Peru: Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Titicaca” tour](/peru/tour/peru-8-days/) includes Chinchero within a broader itinerary introducing travelers to Inca heritage. When choosing a tour, check how much time is allocated to the workshop and archaeological area, and whether the visit coincides with the Sunday market.

## Practical advice

The high plateau can be windy even in sunny weather. Bring warm clothing, UV protection and comfortable footwear for stone paths and the uneven surfaces of the archaeological complex. If you have recently arrived from a low-altitude region, allow for how you may feel at altitude.

Ideally, set aside at least a few hours to explore Chinchero. A quick stop at the market stalls provides little insight into why the settlement matters to local history and culture.

## Frequently asked questions about Chinchero

### Where is Chinchero?

In a high-altitude area northwest of Cusco, near the Sacred Valley.

### When does the famous market operate?

On Sundays. Some workshops and shops open on other days, but the market experience is different.

### What remains from the Inca era?

Terraces, stone foundations and elements of the complex associated with Túpac Yupanqui. Colonial buildings were later constructed nearby and on top of some of the older structures.

### Can I buy traditional textiles?

Yes, from local artisans and at the market. Ask the individual seller about the material composition and purchase terms.

## Adding Chinchero to your Peru journey

[Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/) lies near [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), in the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) area. It brings together archaeological remains, colonial architecture and living weaving traditions. However, the fact that it appears among possible places to visit does not mean the stop is part of the mandatory itinerary.

On the [“Discover Peru & Colombia” journey](/multi-country/tour/peru-colombia-discovery/), day 5 offers free time in Cusco or an optional Sacred Valley excursion. The [“Discover Peru + Iquitos” tour](/peru/tour/peru-iquitos-discovery/) offers a similar choice on day 4. In both cases, the valley excursion can be booked separately without giving up the main visits to Machu Picchu and other itinerary highlights.

The separate [“Sacred Valley of the Incas” excursion](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-of-the-incas-tour/) lists [Urubamba](/peru/place/urubamba/), [Pisac](/peru/place/pisac/), [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/), Chinchero, [Moray](/peru/place/moray/) and the Awanakancha center. This makes it possible to experience Chinchero as part of a full day rather than as an isolated short stop with no onward logistics.

## What an optional Sacred Valley excursion adds

You can spend a free day in Cusco without lengthy transfers: explore the city, rest after exposure to altitude and choose museums independently. A valley excursion expands the geography of the trip and lets you compare different forms of Inca heritage.

| Place | What to see |
|---|---|
| [Pisac](/peru/place/pisac/) | Archaeological complex |
| [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/) | Stone terraces and streets |
| [Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/) | Weaving and architecture |
| [Moray](/peru/place/moray/) | Circular agricultural terraces |

In Chinchero, the highlights are the remains of Inca-period structures, a colonial church and artisan workshops. Learning about local textiles reveals how traditional patterns and techniques remain part of daily life, not merely museum displays. Moray has a different emphasis: using the terrain and complex stone terraces for agriculture.

Travel between these sites takes up part of the day. It is therefore important to establish **which places are actually included in the confirmed excursion option**, how much time is allocated to Chinchero and whether there is time for an unhurried visit to the weaving workshops. A general excursion's list of attractions does not replace a specific daily itinerary with departure and return times.

## Which current tours allow you to add Chinchero?

The [“Discover Peru & Colombia” tour](/multi-country/tour/peru-colombia-discovery/) combines Andean heritage and Lake Titicaca with Bogotá and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). The optional Sacred Valley visit falls on a free day in Cusco. The optional excursion costs **$225** and includes a buffet lunch. The exact sites visited in the valley should be confirmed along with the complete program for that additional day.

After its Andean section, the [“Discover Peru + Iquitos” tour](/peru/tour/peru-iquitos-discovery/) continues to [Iquitos](/peru/place/iquitos/) and the Amazon rainforest. We also offer an optional valley excursion on this itinerary for **$225**, including lunch. It is especially important here to remember that the subsequent days involve flights and a change from a mountain climate to a tropical one. The free day may be valuable for recuperation.

In both cases, **the main tour is a complete experience without the optional Sacred Valley excursion**. If Chinchero is a must-see for you, explore the [tours with Chinchero included in the main itinerary](/peru/place/chinchero/tour/), where the visit is part of the actual route rather than an optional use of free time.

## Planning the day without overloading it

Cusco sits at considerable altitude. When choosing an excursion that visits several valley sites, consider how you feel after arriving, the duration of transfers and the days still ahead. Check the selected tour and excursion terms for exact departure and hotel return times, the guide, lunch, admission tickets and the possibility of additional stops.

Chinchero is worth visiting for its combination of history and contemporary craft culture. If ancient engineering is your main interest, distribute your time between [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/) and [Moray](/peru/place/moray/). If you would like to see traditional weaving, ask how much time is planned for Chinchero. With only one free day, prioritize these interests instead of expecting a detailed visit to every site.

## Frequently asked questions about adding Chinchero

### Is Chinchero included in the “Discover Peru” tours?

On the [“Discover Peru & Colombia”](/multi-country/tour/peru-colombia-discovery/) and [“Discover Peru + Iquitos”](/peru/tour/peru-iquitos-discovery/) itineraries, Chinchero is part of a possible optional Sacred Valley excursion. It is not a required stop on the main itinerary days.

### Does the trip from Cusco take a full day?

The described [Sacred Valley excursion](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-of-the-incas-tour/) covers several settlements and archaeological complexes. The actual duration and order of stops are confirmed when booking; it is more than a short visit to Chinchero alone.

### How much does adding the Sacred Valley cost?

The optional excursion costs **$225** on the two itineraries mentioned. This is the price for this particular option, not a universal rate for every excursion in Chinchero. Check the scope of services and pricing basis for your chosen tour.

### Can I keep my free day in Cusco?

Yes. Both itineraries allow you to choose between resting in Cusco and taking the optional Sacred Valley excursion. If acclimatizing and maintaining a relaxed pace are priorities, keeping the free day is a perfectly valid option.

## Tours through Chinchero: choosing the right itinerary

**[Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/) is usually visited during a sightseeing day in the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/).** Inca ruins, a colonial church and artisan workshops sit close together here. Depending on the itinerary, travelers explore the archaeological complex, discover local textiles or enjoy both experiences.

Our catalog features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The main difference between them is not the Chinchero stop itself, but the length of the journey, the onward destinations and the services explicitly included. Chinchero appears in short trips around Cusco as well as routes extending to Lake Titicaca, northern Peru, the coast or neighboring countries.

The same day's route often mentions [Moray](/peru/place/moray/), [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/), [Pisac](/peru/place/pisac/) and [Urubamba](/peru/place/urubamba/). However, compare the exact stops and the time allocated to each place in individual tours.

## Short journeys: 6–8 days

For a first introduction to Inca heritage, consider routes that place the Sacred Valley between [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/).

| Tour | Main distinction |
|---|---|
| [Peru in 6 days](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-6-days/) | Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu, the valley |
| [Belmond Hiram Bingham train](/peru/tour/peru-belmond-hiram-bingham-machu-picchu/) | 6 days, a special train journey to Machu Picchu |
| [Ancestral Energy](/peru/tour/peru-ancestral-energy/) | 8 days, archaeology and crafts |
| [Peru and Bolivia](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia/) | 8 days, the valley and Titicaca |

### Six days: Lima, Cusco and Machu Picchu

The [six-day Peru tour](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-6-days/) combines major sights in the capital and Cusco with a visit to Machu Picchu. Chinchero is visited on a Sacred Valley excursion together with Pisac, Ollantaytambo and Moray. This option suits travelers who want to see the main destinations during a short vacation.

Chinchero is one stop on a busy excursion day. The inclusion of the town does not, by itself, mean that a separate weaving workshop or several hours of free time are provided.

### Six days with Belmond Hiram Bingham

The [Belmond Hiram Bingham train itinerary](/peru/tour/peru-belmond-hiram-bingham-machu-picchu/) also visits Chinchero, Moray, Ollantaytambo and Machu Picchu. Its principal confirmed distinction is the Hiram Bingham train and the journey's culinary experiences.

Chinchero remains a Sacred Valley stop. A special train experience does not automatically include private sightseeing at every site or additional services in town. Compare the complete tour descriptions.

### Eight days: discovering Chinchero's crafts

The [“Ancestral Energy” tour](/peru/tour/peru-ancestral-energy/) includes a day titled “Sacred Valley: Chinchero, Moray and Ollantaytambo.” In Chinchero, the itinerary expressly names the archaeological complex, colonial church and traditional methods of dyeing and spinning alpaca wool.

On the [“Peru and Bolivia” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia/), Chinchero is likewise associated with a local textile center, the work of artisans, the archaeological complex and the church. The journey then proceeds to Moray and Ollantaytambo, followed by the highlands and Lake Titicaca on subsequent days.

If weaving traditions matter more to you than the total number of attractions, choose itineraries **that explicitly name the textile center**. Watching a demonstration and taking a practical hands-on class are different experiences; the latter should not be assumed without a specific inclusion.

## Longer itineraries across Peru and several countries

Chinchero appears on extended journeys, but it is important to consider how much time is actually spent in the Cusco region.

The [“Complete Peru + Tumbes Beaches” tour](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/) combines Inca heritage with southern regions and a beach stay at the end. The [14-day itinerary featuring Chiclayo](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-arequipa-puno-trujillo-chiclayo/) adds Lake Titicaca, Colca Canyon, Arequipa and the archaeology of northern Peru to the Sacred Valley. Chinchero is one stop in an extensive route on both tours.

On the [Chile, Bolivia and Peru journey](/multi-country/tour/chile-bolivia-peru-vip/), the Sacred Valley and Chinchero come after other high-altitude regions of South America. The [15-day Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) includes Chinchero on its Peru leg. The total length of a multi-country tour should not be confused with the number of days spent in Peru.

The [Brazil–Peru–Argentina group itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/) specifically includes learning how alpaca wool is dyed and spun at Chinchero's textile center, as well as visiting its archaeological complex and colonial church. This is a meaningful difference to consider when comparing journeys.

## Why visit Chinchero?

### Archaeology and a church built on ancient foundations

Chinchero has stone walls and terraces surviving from the pre-Hispanic settlement. Its archaeological park preserves traces of several eras: pre-Inca communities, Inca-period structures and later colonial buildings. The site is protected by Peru's Ministry of Culture.

Several of our tours include the archaeological complex and colonial church. It is especially easy here to see how a settlement developed over time, as new buildings appeared beside ancient stone walls and on top of some earlier structures.

### Textile traditions

Chinchero is renowned for craftswomen who work with wool, traditional dyes and patterned fabrics. A visit to a textile center can give travelers a look at finished products and the processes used to prepare the fibers. Some tour itineraries explicitly include this experience; for others, it needs to be confirmed separately.

A visit to a market or textile shop, a spinning demonstration and a full practical workshop differ in duration and content. Travelers should not expect hands-on participation in making fabric unless the service is clearly described.

## Chinchero, Moray and Ollantaytambo: how do they differ?

The Sacred Valley's neighboring attractions complement one another, which is why they are often visited on the same day.

| Place | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| [Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/) | Textiles, Inca walls, church |
| [Moray](/peru/place/moray/) | Circular agricultural terraces |
| [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/) | Stone structures, town layout |
| [Pisac](/peru/place/pisac/) | Hillside ruins, market |

Moray illustrates farming in different altitude conditions. Ollantaytambo is notable for its preserved stone structures and town layout. Chinchero adds a living weaving tradition to the region's history.

If you want to explore all of these places in depth, compare the sightseeing days of the tours you are considering. The term “Sacred Valley” alone is too general: it can refer to different stops and activities.

## Altitude and planning the excursion day

Chinchero lies in the highlands of the Cusco region. The archaeological park is located at approximately **3,785 meters** above sea level. Traveling from coastal Lima to this altitude calls for attention to acclimatization, particularly during the first days after arrival in the Andes.

On most confirmed itineraries, travelers visit Chinchero during the day along with other Sacred Valley sites rather than spending the night there. When evaluating a tour, consider the time needed for travel, archaeological sightseeing and the textile center. Anyone hoping to spend several hours learning about weaving should arrange a longer stop in advance.

Further journeys in this region can be found in the [Sacred Valley tour catalog](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/tour/). You can also compare [cultural and historical tours in Peru](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/).

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting Chinchero

### Can I visit Chinchero on a day trip from Cusco?

Yes. On several current itineraries, Chinchero is part of a one-day Sacred Valley excursion. However, that stop is **included within a longer tour**, rather than offered as a universal standalone trip on any date.

### Which tour lets me see traditional weaving?

An introduction to local textile traditions is explicitly included in [“Ancestral Energy”](/peru/tour/peru-ancestral-energy/), [“Peru and Bolivia”](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia/) and the [three-country group tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-peru-argentina-group-15-days/).

### Is there a short trip featuring both Chinchero and Machu Picchu?

Yes. The [six-day Peru tour](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-6-days/) includes both places. Another itinerary of the same length is the [journey featuring the Hiram Bingham train](/peru/tour/peru-belmond-hiram-bingham-machu-picchu/).

### Do all itineraries offer the same Chinchero excursion?

No. Some descriptions name only the archaeological complex and the church, while others also include the textile center. Compare the details of the day and the surrounding stops.

### Is it worth spending an entire day in Chinchero?

A basic introduction usually takes part of an excursion day. Exploring the crafts and history more deeply requires additional time and an agreed change to the itinerary.

## Chivay, Peru: gateway to Colca Canyon and its hot springs

Chivay is a town in the high-altitude Colca Valley of southern Peru. Many routes from [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/) to [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/) pass through it. Travelers stop here and spend the night before an early departure for the viewpoints, while also experiencing everyday life in a small Andean town.

The landscape around Chivay is very different from Peru's coast: dry hillsides, mountain pastures, agricultural terraces and valley settlements. The town is also known for its proximity to the La Calera hot springs.

## Why stop in Chivay?

For many travelers, Chivay is a convenient base before visiting Cruz del Cóndor, a lookout where Andean condors can be seen soaring above the canyon. It is possible to visit the canyon from Arequipa in a single day, but the drive is long. Spending the night in Chivay lets travelers divide the journey into more manageable stages.

In town, you can walk along central streets, see local architecture and have lunch before continuing. The time and activities depend on the tour format. Do not confuse visiting Chivay with undertaking a full trek through the canyon: hiking routes along its slopes require separate preparation.

## La Calera hot springs

The La Calera thermal pools are located near Chivay and are a popular place to unwind after traveling. Peru's official tourism portal includes the springs among the main attractions of the Colca area.

Thermal facilities have their own visitor rules and health restrictions. Water temperature, recommended bathing time and facilities can vary. For some travelers, bathing in hot water at high altitude warrants advice from a health professional.

The [SPA and wellness travel collection](/interests/spa/) offers other ways to relax. However, the presence of hot springs near Chivay does not mean thermal bathing is automatically included in every Colca Canyon tour.

## Cruz del Cóndor and birdwatching

Cruz del Cóndor is a famous lookout over Colca Canyon. In the morning, Andean condors may glide above the gorge, riding rising currents of air. These large birds sometimes fly close to the viewpoints, but sightings depend on the weather and the animals' natural activity.

The canyon itself is impressive in scale: steep slopes, terraces and mountain ledges reveal the complex terrain of the southern Andes. Photographers should allow enough time and bring a suitable lens; never cross safety barriers to get a shot.

The canyon is a protected tourism area, and local fees and admission conditions should be considered separately from the cost of accommodation and transfers.

## The road from Arequipa

According to Peru's official tourism portal, the journey from Arequipa to Chivay covers about 150 km and takes approximately 3–3.5 hours. The altitude and mountain roads make the drive demanding. Reaching the canyon viewpoints requires an additional transfer.

| Route section | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Arequipa–Chivay | Transfer to the Colca Valley |
| Chivay–La Calera | Relaxation at the hot springs |
| Chivay–Cruz del Cóndor | Scenic views and birdwatching |

The exact travel time depends on the route, stops and road conditions. If the excursion also includes villages, agricultural terraces or viewpoints, the day can become quite long.

## Chivay on Peru tours

On the [“Lima, Cusco, Titicaca, Colca and Arequipa” journey](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-titicaca-colca-arequipa-nazca/), Chivay is part of a longer itinerary through the southern Andes. On the [“Complete Peru and Tumbes Beaches” tour](/peru/tour/complete-peru-tumbes-beaches/), the Colca Valley also complements the country's cultural and natural destinations.

When comparing programs, check whether an overnight stay in Chivay is included, how much time is allocated to Cruz del Cóndor and whether visits to the hot springs are specifically scheduled. Such details have a greater effect on the experience than the mere presence of the word “Colca” in the tour title.

## Altitude, weather and clothing

Chivay is located in the highlands. After traveling from coastal Lima or lower valleys, be alert to symptoms of altitude adjustment, avoid excessive physical exertion on the first day and follow medical advice if you have health conditions. The morning viewpoints can be cold even in sunny weather.

A warm jacket, sunglasses, a hat and comfortable shoes will be useful. Stay on marked paths when walking in natural areas.

## Frequently asked questions about Chivay

### Where is Chivay?

In the Colca Valley of southern Peru, in a high-altitude area northwest of Arequipa.

### How long is the drive from Arequipa?

Approximately 3–3.5 hours, excluding all tourist stops.

### Why spend the night in Chivay?

To make an early start for Colca Canyon easier and avoid spending the entire day on lengthy transfers.

### Are there hot springs?

Yes. The La Calera thermal pools are nearby. Whether a visit is included depends on the specific excursion.
